posts.body:

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.127.0 (Universal)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)

Steps to Reproduce:

## Bug Description

After upgrading VS Code, all previous Copilot Chat session history is completely
gone from the Chat History panel. No warning, no migration, no recovery option.

## Root Cause (Observed)

The Copilot Chat extension changed its chat session storage format from `.json` to
`.jsonl` between versions. Sessions in the old `.json` format still exist on disk at:

~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/workspaceStorage/<hash>/chatSessions/<uuid>.json

...but the new extension silently ignores them. They are never read, migrated, or
displayed in the UI.

Related: #307761 (chat history not loading from .jsonl files — different root cause, closed as not planned)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use VS Code Copilot Chat for multiple sessions across several workspaces
2. Upgrade VS Code to a version that changed the session format to `.jsonl`
3. Open VS Code and check the Chat History panel
4. All prior sessions are gone

## Expected Behavior

One of:
- The extension **migrates** existing `.json` session files to `.jsonl` on first run after upgrade
- The extension **reads both formats** for backward compatibility
- Users are shown a **warning** before upgrading and offered an export/backup option

## Actual Behavior

Previous chat sessions vanish silently. No warning, no migration, no recovery UI.
Months of conversation context (debugging sessions, architectural decisions, code
explanations) is permanently lost.

## Impact

- Sessions represent significant complex work context that cannot easily be reconstructed
- The change was made without any migration path, user notice, or changelog callout

## Environment

- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (25F80)
- Old format: `.json` (files still present on disk, confirmed)
- New format: `.jsonl`

## Requested Fix

Add a one-time startup migration that converts `.json` chat sessions to `.jsonl`,
or at minimum add a "Restore legacy sessions" command to the Command Palette.

posts.title: Renderer crash (EMFILE / Too many open files in platform_channel.cc) when opening a new window, reported as opaque 'clean-exit'
posts.body:
GitHub issue #326149
Status: open
Created: 2026-07-16T12:22:23Z
Updated: 2026-07-16T13:23:25Z

### Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?
Not tested with extensions disabled — root cause identified below is independent of any specific extension.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run VS Code on Linux with a systemd-managed user session where `DefaultLimitNOFILESoft=1024` (this is systemd's own default on Ubuntu and most modern distros; hard limit is typically much higher, e.g. `524288`).
2. Keep a normal multi-window workflow running for a while (several windows, extension hosts, language servers, terminal processes, docker/LSP sockets, etc.) so the process tree's open file descriptor count grows over the session.
3. Open an additional new window/workspace.
4. The new renderer process fails to start and VS Code shows: **"The window terminated unexpectedly (reason: 'clean-exit', code: '0')"**.

This reproduced repeatedly (5 times in ~40 minutes) specifically at the moment of creating a *new* window, which is the point where a renderer needs to establish several new Mojo IPC channels at once.

### Root cause (confirmed via Crashpad minidump)

Crashpad captured an actual dump for one of the crashes (`--type=renderer`, `--ozone-platform=wayland`). Extracting readable strings from it shows the real fatal error, which VS Code's main process then logs as an innocuous "clean-exit, code 0":

```
[139697:0100/000000.964368:FATAL:mojo/public/cpp/platform/platform_channel.cc:150] Check failed: . : Too many open files (24)
```

This is `EMFILE` — the renderer process itself hit its **soft** `RLIMIT_NOFILE` (1024) while trying to create a new Mojo platform channel (socketpair) at startup, even though the **hard** limit was 524288 and plenty of headroom existed system-wide.

Two things make this easy to hit on current VS Code/Electron builds:
- The renderer's command line has `--enable-features=...,EarlyEstablishGpuChannel,EstablishGpuChannelAsync,GlobalShortcutsPortal,...` enabled — these establish extra IPC/GPU channels (and, on Wayland, extra D-Bus portal connections for global shortcuts) earlier and more eagerly during window startup than before, increasing the peak fd count right at the moment a new window is created.
- VS Code/Electron does not raise its own soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` toward the process's hard limit at startup (many other Electron/Node apps do call `setrlimit()` early to raise the soft limit to the hard limit when the hard limit allows it).

Because the failure is a hard `CHECK` inside Mojo, the renderer process aborts instantly with exit code 0 and no user-facing error text — the main process just reports `renderer process gone (reason: clean-exit, code: <unknown>)` and shows the generic "terminated unexpectedly" dialog, which makes this very hard for users to diagnose without pulling the Crashpad `.dmp` and grepping strings for `FATAL`.

### Why this seems tied to a recent update

The systemd soft limit of 1024 is not new — it's a long-standing Ubuntu/systemd default. What changed for us was the VS Code version: this started happening consistently after updating from 1.125.1 → 1.129.0 (via apt: 1.125.1 → 1.127.0 → 1.128.0 → 1.128.1 → 1.129.0). The `EarlyEstablishGpuChannel`/`EstablishGpuChannelAsync` feature flags visible in the crashed renderer's command line are relatively recent Chromium features bundled with the Electron bump in this range, which plausibly increased the number of fds opened per window at startup, pushing already fd-heavy sessions (multiple windows, extension hosts, language servers, docker) over the 1024 soft-limit ceiling that previously had headroom.

### Suggested fix

- Have the Electron/main process raise its own soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` toward the hard limit at startup (`setrlimit(RLIMIT_NOFILE, {soft: hard, hard: hard})`) when the hard limit allows it, instead of relying on the OS/session default of 1024. This is a common and safe mitigation used by other high-fd-usage Linux daemons/apps.
- At minimum, surface the real Mojo/Chromium fatal reason (e.g. "Too many open files") in the "terminated unexpectedly" dialog instead of the opaque `clean-exit` reason, so users aren't stuck reverse-engineering Crashpad dumps to find an `EMFILE`.

### Environment

- VS Code version: 1.129.0 (commit `125df4672b8a6a34975303c6b0baa124e560a4f7`), previously reproduced across 1.127.0/1.128.0/1.128.1 as well
- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Linux kernel (Wayland session, `--ozone-platform=wayland`)
- `ulimit -n` for the affected session: soft `1024`, hard `524288` (systemd `DefaultLimitNOFILESoft=1024` — distro default, not customized)
- Workaround that resolved it for us: raising `DefaultLimitNOFILESoft` via a systemd user-manager drop-in (`/etc/systemd/user.conf.d/limits.conf`, `DefaultLimitNOFILE=65536:524288`) followed by a full logout/login. This is an OS-level workaround; VS Code itself doesn't need to rely on the caller having done this.

The turn's preamble text and tool-invocation lines render, then the message-control buttons (retry/copy/thumbs) appear — but the assistant's concluding text (summaries, tables, results) never displays. The work itself completes on the backend (files are written, commits made, memory updated); only the closing rendered text is lost. ## Environment - **VS Code:** 1.128.0-insider - **GitHub Copilot Chat extension:** 0.56.2026070703 (issue also observed on 0.56.2026070103 earlier in the same session) - **Model:** Claude Opus 4.8 (agent mode) - **OS:** Windows - **Chat session id:** cc9f1423-422d-41c7-a725-c5aa9494c46c ## Impact - Users cannot see task results/summaries even though the actions succeeded. - Creates false impression the agent "went silent" or stalled. - Erodes trust; forces manual verification of whether work actually completed. ## Steps to reproduce 1. In Copilot Chat agent mode, ask for a task that (a) invokes one or more tools (search, file edit, terminal, or memory), then (b) concludes with a substantive text summary (e.g., a table or multi-item list). 2. Observe the turn: preamble and tool lines render, then the control buttons appear. 3. Intermittently, the concluding assistant text is missing entirely. ## Actual result Final assistant text (summary/table) is not rendered; turn ends on the control buttons. ## Expected result The full final assistant message renders and persists in the transcript. ## Frequency / pattern (observed 2026-07-07, single session) Confirmed drops: 3. Clean turns: 2. | Turn | Tool calls before final text? | Final text rendered? | |------|-------------------------------|----------------------| | "list hardcoded model versions in agents" (search) | Yes | **No (dropped)** | | Re-delivery of same content | No (text only) | Yes | | "is size the cause?" reasoning | No (text only) | Yes | | Time-bound workaround setup (2 memory writes) | Yes | **No (dropped)** | **Correlation:** every confirmed drop occurred on a turn that emits final text *after* tool calls in the same turn. The two clean turns were text-only. It is **intermittent** (not every tool-call turn drops), and it is **not content/size dependent** — the identical payload that dropped once rendered perfectly on retry. ## Additional anomalies 1. **Mid-session extension auto-update + repeated session re-init.** The session debug log records multiple `session_start` events for the *same* session id, and the Copilot version changed mid-session (0.56.2026070103 → 0.56.2026070703). A restart did not resolve the drops, which continue on the stable version. 2. **Native Todos panel showed a stale count.** On the memory-write turn the Todos panel displayed "1/2" complete when both tasks had in fact completed (2/2). ## Evidence to attach - Screenshots of the affected turns (preamble present, final text absent, controls shown; Todos panel showing 1/2). - Session debug log: `%APPDATA%\Code - Insiders\User\workspaceStorage\22362043cdd10fe935dd5f7a1e081b72\GitHub.copilot-chat\debug-logs\cc9f1423-422d-41c7-a725-c5aa9494c46c\main.jsonl` (contains the repeated `session_start` events and version change). ## Workaround in use - Ending each turn with a sentinel line so its absence flags a drop. - Preferring text-only turns for substantive summaries (decoupling summaries from tool-call turns). - Verifying actual artifact state (files/commits) rather than trusting the Todos panel count. ## Notes This is a rendering/streaming/transcript-persistence issue on the client side, not a model generation failure — the backend actions complete and the content is generated; only the final rendered assistant message is lost. GitHub issue #326152 Status: open Created: 2026-07-16T12:43:09Z Updated: 2026-07-16T12:51:48Z Type: Bug 1. Create a new VS Code extension with this minimal package.json: ``` { "name": "tool-test", "displayName": "bar", "publisher": "foo", "version": "0.0.1", "engines": { "vscode": "^1.99.0" }, "main": "./src/index.js", "contributes": { "languageModelTools": [ { "name": "tool_1", "displayName": "Test Tool 1", "toolReferenceName": "testTool1", "canBeReferencedInPrompt": true, "modelDescription": "A minimal test tool.", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {} } } ] } } ``` 2. ## Use Case / Problem Description

I have a Python script running inside a remote Linux Dev Container (connected via Remote - SSH / Dev Containers from a Windows host). The script is executed by a Git pre-commit hook and generates a short string.

I would like this string to be automatically copied to the local Windows clipboard so that the developer can immediately paste it (`Ctrl+V`) in the next step, without manually selecting and copying text from the terminal.

## What I Tried

### 1. OSC 52 Escape Sequences

I enabled:

```json
"terminal.integrated.enableOsc52": true
```

and emitted:

```text
\033]52;c;<base64>\a
```

from the Python script.

While this occasionally works in an interactive terminal session, it does not work reliably when executed from a Git pre-commit hook or another non-interactive process launched through VS Code's Source Control workflow. The OSC 52 sequence appears to be swallowed or never forwarded to the local Windows client.

### 2. `vscode.env.clipboard.writeText()`

This API is only available inside the VS Code extension runtime and therefore cannot be used by standalone CLI scripts or Git hooks running inside the container.

### 3. Standard Linux Utilities (`xclip`, `xsel`, `clip.exe`)

- `xclip` and `xsel` require an active X server, which is unavailable in a headless Dev Container.
- `clip.exe` is a Windows executable and is not accessible from within the remote Linux container.

## Proposed Solution

It would be helpful to support one of the following mechanisms:

### Option A: VS Code CLI Clipboard Command

Provide a command such as:

```bash
code --clipboard-write "text"
```

that securely bridges clipboard operations from the remote environment to the local host, similar to how `code .` can interact with the local VS Code instance.

### Option B: Reliable OSC 52 Forwarding

Ensure that OSC 52 sequences emitted by Git hooks, subprocesses, and other background processes running in the integrated terminal are consistently intercepted and forwarded to the host clipboard.

### Option C: IPC or Environment-Based Bridge

Provide a documented IPC mechanism (socket, command, or environment variable) that allows scripts running inside Dev Containers or Remote SSH sessions to send simple payloads, such as clipboard content, back to the local VS Code client.

## Environment

- **Host OS:** Windows 10/11
- **Remote Environment:** Linux (Ubuntu) in a Dev Container / Remote SSH session
- **VS Code Setting:**

```json
"terminal.integrated.enableOsc52": true
```

## Additional Context

Clipboard access from scripts and Git hooks is a common requirement for developer workflows that generate tokens, IDs, migration names, commit metadata, or other short values that need to be pasted immediately into another tool. Currently, there is no supported and reliable mechanism for transferring clipboard data from a remote container back to the local host.
posts.subject: Support writing to the local clipboard from Dev Containers and Remote SSH sessions

posts.title: Copilot Chat 0.43.0: Claude agent mode silent — tool permission stream closes before response received (hook_6)
posts.body:
GitHub issue #308999
Status: closed
Created: 2026-04-10T11:58:48Z
Updated: 2026-07-16T11:57:40Z

Type: **Bug**

## Summary

When running Copilot Chat in **Claude agent mode**, the chat window is silent during any turn that requires tool calls. The VS Code output panel logs a specific error from the claude-agent-sdk: the tool permission hook stream (`hook_6`) closes before the permission decision arrives, aborting the tool call before any response can be generated. This started approximately 27 March 2026 and has been consistently reproducible since.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open VS Code (1.115) with GitHub Copilot Chat 0.43.0.
2. In Copilot Chat, switch to Claude agent mode (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4.6`).
3. Issue any prompt that requires tool use — file reads, web fetches, shell commands, or git operations.
4. Observe that the chat window shows no activity and no response while the agent is working.
5. Open the VS Code output panel and filter to the Copilot Chat output channel.

## Expected Behaviour

The agent narrates progress and shows tool call activity in the chat window throughout the turn. A final response is delivered when the turn completes.

## Actual Behaviour

The chat window is silent throughout. The output panel logs one or more instances of:

```
[error] claude-agent-sdk stderr: Error in hook callback hook_6: Error: Tool permission stream closed before response received
    at F58.read (file:///home/ciara/.vscode-server/extensions/github.copilot-chat-0.43.0/dist/cli.js:8246:342)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:103:5)
    at async file:///home/ciara/.vscode-server/extensions/github.copilot-chat-0.43.0/dist/cli.js:16742:1569
```

The claude-agent-sdk receives no tool permission response and aborts the tool call. Because the turn never completes, no output is generated for the chat window.

## Session Log Evidence

The Copilot Chat debug log (exported via "Export All Prompts as JSON") shows the symptom directly.

**ChatMLCancelation — aborted turn (duration 157 ms, no work done):**
```json
{
  "id": "37bfd4cc",
  "kind": "request",
  "type": "ChatMLCancelation",
  "name": "Claude Copilot Proxy",
  "metadata": {
    "requestType": "ChatMessages",
    "model": "claude-sonnet-4.6",
    "startTime": "2026-04-10T11:35:40.129Z",
    "endTime": "2026-04-10T11:35:40.286Z",
    "duration": 157
  }
}
```

**Multiple empty-response turns in the same session** (ids: `4d5a311f`, `a799007f`, `51c1061c`) — turns where Claude responded with an empty message because the tool call it depended on was never completed.

**Contrast:** Turns where no tool call was needed completed normally and their responses were relayed to the chat window without issue. The failure is specific to the tool permission stage, not to text relay.

## Analysis

The tool permission hook system in the claude-agent-sdk uses a stream (`hook_6`) to deliver the allow/deny decision for each tool call. That stream is closing before the decision arrives. Possible causes:

1. **Timing regression** — the permission decision now arrives after a threshold that causes the read stream to time out or be garbage-collected.
2. **`use-responses-api` experiment interaction** — two previously closed related issues (#297982, #297879) both had the `use-responses-api` A/B experiment active. If switching from the streaming completions API to the Responses API changes the timing or lifecycle of hook callbacks, this could cause premature stream closure.
3. **SDK version mismatch** — a version incompatibility between the claude-agent-sdk bundled in `cli.js` and the callback contract expected by the extension host.

The obfuscated symbol `F58.read` at `cli.js:8246:342` is the stream reader for the hook callback; the async dispatch at `cli.js:16742:1569` is the main agent loop awaiting the permission result.

## Onset

The problem began approximately **27 March 2026**, coinciding with the VS Code 1.113 release cycle. VS Code 1.113 introduced bridging of MCP servers to Claude agent sessions and changed session listing to use the official Claude agent SDK API. None of the 1.113–1.115 release notes document a change to tool permission or hook callback handling, suggesting the cause may be a server-side experiment rollout rather than a VS Code binary change.

## Related Issues

- microsoft/vscode#297982 — Copilot Chat incorrectly stating MCP tools unavailable (closed not_planned; had `use-responses-api` experiment active)
- microsoft/vscode#297879 — Unable to access any available MCP (closed not_planned; had `use-responses-api` experiment active)

## Environment

Extension version: **0.43.0**
VS Code version: **1.115** (released 2026-04-07)
OS: **Linux x64** (WSL2, kernel 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2)
Running in: VS Code Server (remote/Codespace)

<details>
<summary>System Info</summary>

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Shell | bash |
| Remote | VS Code Server on Linux WSL2 |
| Extension host | github.copilot-chat-0.43.0 |
| claude-agent-sdk | bundled in dist/cli.js |

</details>

posts.body:
GitHub issue #312446
Status: closed

## VS Code Version
Insiders (commit f2b51f3f64)

## OS
Windows

## Copilot Chat Extension
Latest (bundled with Insiders)

## Description

When the agent calls the screenshot_page browser tool (or any tool that returns image data), the extension fails to construct a valid multimodal request payload. The API rejects it with:

`
400 {"error":{"code":"400","message":"Param Incorrect","param":"text is not set","type":""}}
`

The error trace points to _provideLanguageModelResponse in xtension.js:

`
at Dj._provideLanguageModelResponse (c:\Users\xdoomx\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders\f2b51f3f64\resources\app\extensions\copilot\dist\extension.js:1699:12529)
`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Copilot Chat (Agent mode)
2. Ask the agent to take a screenshot of any browser page (e.g., "screenshot the current page")
3. The agent calls screenshot_page
4. The tool returns image data to the model
5. The extension fails to wrap the image result with a text part in the multimodal payload

## Expected Behavior

The tool result should be sent as a properly formatted multimodal message containing both the image data and a text part (even an empty or descriptive string), so the API accepts it.

## Actual Behavior

The image is sent without a 	ext field, causing the API to reject the request with a 400 error.

## Root Cause (Likely)

The tool-to-model pipeline for image-returning tools does not include the required 	ext property in the content array. The API requires at least one 	ext part alongside any image part.

## Impact

Any tool that returns image data to the model is broken in agent mode. This includes screenshot_page, iew_image, and potentially custom MCP tools that return images.

## Workaround

Use ead_page (DOM snapshot) instead of screenshot_page for browser inspection. This avoids the image-handling path entirely.
